text:
harper: heads-up — short spike in p99 for dedicated-usw2 chat models since ~15:03. small-token gen latency doubled. looks like route recalcs on the pool-router coinciding with a tenant doing huge concurrent exports. anyone seen router churn like this?
sam: seeing router recalculation events for pool-router-usw2. which tenant(s)?
harper: racks r2/r3. quick logs: 
```
2026-09-14T15:02:57Z pool-router[pr-4]: route_recalc reason=topology-change affected=14ms
2026-09-14T15:03:01Z shard-proxy[sp-9]: egress_bytes tenant=acct-710 delta=200MB/s iface=tor-eth0 burst=true
2026-09-14T15:03:02Z allocator[al-2]: prefill_fanout tenant=acct-855 parallel=6 crossrack=true
```
harper: acct-710 is a bulk export, acct-855 was fractionally promoted earlier and is doing aggressive multi-rack warms. the router recalcs are causing short path flaps and cache misses in proxies, amplifying latency.
nidhi: interesting — we haven't seen route_recalc amplify into p99 like this. maybe the router's sticky-cache TTL is too short under churn. also prefill_fanout=6 is high for cross-rack warms.
oncall-sre: i'm oncall. short mitigation plan: 1) enable router anti-flap mode (increases sticky cache TTL and batches recalcs for 30s), 2) apply per-tenant soft-egress-cap (token-bucket) for acct-710 to 60MB/s, 3) reduce allocator prefill_fanout_limit to 2 for the pool. can ops run commands?
ops-automation: commands ready: 
```bash
# router anti-flap (feature rsdb: router-stabilizer)
rctl config set prod pool-router router_stabilizer=true
rctl config set prod pool-router router_stabilizer_batch_ms=30000
# per-tenant soft egress cap
rctl tenant update acct-710 --egress_cap_bytes_per_sec=62914560 --note="temp-soft-cap"
# limiter for prefill fanout
rctl config set prod allocator prefill_fanout_limit=2
```
sam: before flipping router flags, can we check how many route_recalc events in last 10m and correlate with proxy cache misses? quick query: 
```sql
SELECT count(*) FROM infra.router_events WHERE event='route_recalc' AND time > now() - 10m;
SELECT sum(cache_miss) FROM shard.proxy_cache_stats WHERE time > now() - 10m AND pool='dedicated-usw2';
```
sam: ran it  7 recalcs in 10m and proxy cache_miss spiked concurrently. looks correlated.
harper: ok ops-automation apply the router stabilizer and lower fanout. tag me when done.
ops-automation: applied router_stabilizer=true and batch_ms=30000; set prefill_fanout_limit=2; tenant acct-710 egress_cap applied. infra-bot: recorded changes user=oncall-sre action=set router_stabilizer=true at=2026-09-14T15:06:12Z
oncall-sre: monitoring p99 and router event rate. please keep an eye on shard proxy miss rate.
nidhi: watching — p99 dropped from ~260ms to ~120ms within 50s; proxy cache misses reduced significantly. acct-855 prefill rate dropped with fanout limit. acct-710 egress down to ~55MB/s.
billing-bot: ops noted provisional excess egress for acct-710 (~1.1TB). billing will hold charge pending post-incident review.
sam: follow-ups: 1) add an alert for route_recalc rate > 3 in 5m for pool-router services; 2) make prefill_fanout_limit a per-pool config with sane defaults (2) and a guard that refuses >3 when router_stabilizer=false; 3) add proxy_cache_miss metric to the SLO dashboard. i'll file infra tickets.
harper: medium-term idea: scheduler should include a "control-plane impact" check before multi-rack warms — if predicted router churn or proxy cache miss > threshold, reduce warmup aggression. also consider a transient backpressure signal from routers to schedulers (router->allocator backoff message).
oncall-sre: +1 on backpressure signal. also request that tenant promotions include a pre-check that estimates control-plane impact (prefill_fanout * estimated_conn_count).
nidhi: i'll draft a short RFC for router stabilizer defaults, fanout guards, and a backpressure topic. would be good to include cost-guardrails in promo flow too.
oncall-sre: closing loop for now. ping here if it reappears. :thumbsup:
